subject.title: fix(scripts): bound gh CLI helper subprocess calls

question: Should every `plain-gh` helper call fail after 30 seconds by default, or should deadlines be selected by operation type and caller intent?
rationale: The correct timeout is an operational policy choice because this shared helper serves both quick API reads and potentially longer maintainer automation, and the PR does not establish that one deadline is safe for all callers.

options.title: Classify callers first
options.body: Audit callers, retain a bounded default for short API operations, and set explicit longer or disabled deadlines for commands designed to wait.

options.title: Accept one global deadline
options.body: Adopt 30 seconds for all helpers after adding tests and real proof that representative PR, release, and inherited-stdio operations remain usable.

options.title: Keep caller-owned timeouts
options.body: Do not add a shared default; add deadlines only to specific network operations whose expected duration and failure handling are known.

recommendation.title: Classify callers first
recommendation.body: Audit callers, retain a bounded default for short API operations, and set explicit longer or disabled deadlines for commands designed to wait.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects shared PR and release-maintenance behavior rather than one isolated script call.
